feature: Admin AI assistant that performs tasks

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). Text chat, voice and screen sharing; creates and edits products, content, discounts, segments, reports and Flow workflows; continues longer tasks in the background and notifies when ready; can generate custom apps. Availability varies by plan, device and language; no extra cost stated.

gap: Owner tools plus manager tools (D94, D103 to D105, D153); calls that send, publish, spend or change access are only kept for the owner's yes. D308: it makes and changes products (A1: create_product, update_product, set_prices, set_product_status, write_product_texts, set_stock, through saveProduct()), the website (A2: build_page by the page studio after the answer with its pictures one by one, list_page_builds, edit_page, publish_page, unpublish_page, set_page_place, save_menu, set_header_footer, for a store and for Kaizena Flow's own site, through the builder's and the menu editor's own saves), the setup (A3: set_store_details, set_countries, set_languages, set_currencies, set_flat_shipping, save_shipping_method, open_store, with setup_progress saying what only the owner can do) and themes (A4: list_themes, add_theme, try_theme, make_theme_live, a premium theme only at the charge the owner was shown). D318 (PSI AGT-01, AGT-04): marketing (broadcasts, segments, customer tags, automations, gift cards), support (read, note, reply, end), the team and the plan (owner only, gate `access`), order changes and exchanges, Work, and follow-ups that come back as background turns at their time and email the person where the answer is; an order rule can ask it to look at a paid order. D309: goals with targets measured by code, plans checked against the tools it offers, the autopilot working through them every minute on the maker's yes by the owner's autonomy level and budgets, the Autopilot page and a daily digest and weekly report by email. D310: it photographs a page's draft or the live store and judges it before asking to publish (look_at_page, look_at_store). D311: legal pages written and kept current by the AI (legal_pages_status). D315: domains (search, buy, renew, DNS changes, moves) through domain-tools.ts, buying and DNS behind their gates. Still missing (criterion 3): the owner is told about finished background work only on the Autopilot page, in the conversation or by email; nothing in the admin's header or the assistant's launcher says that a build, follow-up or plan step is ready for review. Merged on 2026-10-25 (README rule 8): `platform.admin-ai-assistant` was the same Shopify feature (rated partial); its criteria and evidence are here.
criteria: The assistant can create and edit a product (title, description, price per market through commerce.set_price, variants, stock) through a gated tool whose approval summary shows the whole change.
The assistant can create, edit and publish a page, and edit a menu, through gated tools that use the same validation as the editors (pageInput, menu rules) and call updateTag.
A long request (for example a bulk change across many products) runs as a background job that survives closing the panel, and the owner is told in the admin when it is ready for review.
A tool that changes a store appears in the store MCP server (D96) too, and the owner-tool coverage test fails when it has no TOOL_WORDS line.
Gated tools create and update a product draft and a page draft; nothing is published or priced without the owner's yes, and the model never states a price or stock it was not given by a tool.
A tool edits a menu and a page's rows through the same validation as the editor (`productInput`, `pageInput`), with every text passing `findClaims()`.
A long job (translating a store, building a page) runs in the background with progress the owner can read, and survives closing the panel.
Each new tool has zod arguments, a `TOOL_WORDS` line and a `gate`, and is served by the store MCP server like the rest.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). "Use text chat, voice mode, or screen sharing to interact with Sidekick."

gap: Evidence debt: hands-free listening by loudness and barge-in are browser code (`voice-mode.ts`, `live-voice.ts`) with no test, and no test covers the path with no speech model; `speech-text.test.ts` holds sentence cutting and `saysYes`, `live-voice.int.test.ts` the server side.
criteria: With a speech model set, voice mode listens hands-free, transcribes, and speaks each answer sentence by sentence; talking over it stops it.

With a live (full-duplex) model set, voice mode is a WebRTC call made by a server route (the key stays on the server) that delegates every request to a normal assistant turn with its tools and approval gate.
A change waiting for approval is approved in words only when the person's own message plainly says yes (saysYes), whatever the model says.
Without a speech or live model configured the assistant says so and text chat still works.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). Learns from past conversations and recent admin activity; a repeated request can be saved as a skill and run again with a shortcut.

gap: Memory is complete: per account, found by keyword and meaning, learned after each turn and from thumbs, shown and editable on the Memory tab, learning can be switched off (D103). Skills are 41 fixed playbooks in code (36 for a store, 5 for the platform; ASSISTANT_SKILLS in src/lib/assistant-skills.ts) loaded by use_skill; there is no table, tool or screen to save a request as a skill, or to edit or delete one.
criteria: An owner can save a conversation's request as a named skill (store or account scope) from the panel, and list, edit and delete their skills.
use_skill loads a saved skill like a built-in one; a saved skill cannot replace a built-in id and cannot hold a secret or a customer's details (the memory filters apply).
A saved skill's steps can only call tools the person may use; gated tools stay gated when a skill runs.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick Pulse). Recommendations on the admin Home; Sidekick also notifies when a background task is ready.

gap: The store's Home shows the top three alerts (eleven kinds: conversion drop, weekday revenue, refund rate, CAC, stock-outs, checkout abandonment, discount creep, targets, cost coverage, good news) with figures and a page to open (D152), the full list is on the Analytics overview and the assistant has analytics_alerts. All of it is worked out on read, in code, from analytics: nothing is pushed (no morning or weekly briefing by email or in the admin), and nothing outside analytics (catalogue, SEO, marketing) is suggested. Since D309 the autopilot emails a weekly report (sales and orders counted in code, goals, an optional checked note) and a daily digest, but only to people whose plans run, not built from the alerts and with no switch of its own.
criteria: A weekly (or daily) briefing is built in code from alertsForStore and the store checkup, sent to owners who switched it on, once per period (idempotent key), and never sent for a quiet store.
Every figure in the briefing is counted in code and each item links to the admin page that acts on it; the model never makes a number.
The owner can switch the briefing off and choose its frequency; a platform admin never receives a store's briefing.
An alert can hand its context to the assistant (open the panel with the alert's figures) to propose a gated next step.

feature: AI product descriptions and SEO text

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). Generates product descriptions and other text from a text icon on admin editing pages; most features at no additional cost, availability varies by plan, device and language.

criteria: In the product editor staff can ask for a write, improve, SEO or translate suggestion; the suggestion fills only the fields of that kind (title, description, SEO title, SEO description) within their limits.
The model is given the product's own words and never prices or stock, and every suggestion passes the claims filter before it can be used.
A suggestion is only shown in the editor for staff to edit and copy in; nothing is written to the product directly, and the log records who asked, never the text.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). Generates images from a text description (reference photos allowed) and saves them; monthly and short-term limits depend on the Shopify plan.

gap: generateImage()/makePicture() (the picture model named in the AI settings, never in code) is used by the AI page studio (src/server/page-ai.ts), the content packs (D257, D270), every picture field of the page builder since D283 (Make with AI and Make again with AI, in the site's look by pictureDirection(), metered as `page_pictures`, kept in the media library with alt text from the request; src/server/picture-maker.ts, /admin/{store}/media/make) and, since D308, the AI manager's create_product, which can make a product's picture from a brief through makeSitePicture(). Still short: (1) the media library and the product editor themselves have no generate-picture action (criterion 1); (2) a made picture is not marked as AI-made in the library, and its alt text (the request's first sentence, altFromBrief()) does not pass the claims filter (criterion 3).
criteria: The media library and the product editor each have a generate-picture action that takes a prompt, uses the store's picture model, shrinks to WebP with a thumbnail and registers the file in the library with alt text.
Without a picture model the action says so and nothing is spent; every call is metered under an AI feature and counts toward the store's usage.
Generated pictures are marked as AI-made in the library and the alt text passes the claims filter.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick and the media file editor). The file editor can replace an image's background; Tinker, a separate free mobile app, offers more than 100 AI tools for images and video.

gap: Text-to-image only: ai.ts calls /images/generations and nothing sends a picture to a model for editing (no background replacement or removal, no cleanup, no variants).
criteria: From a library picture the owner can run an edit (replace or remove the background, and a prompted change) through the provider's image-edit endpoint, set in AI settings.
The result is saved as a new library item and the original is never overwritten; the edit is metered and priced like other picture calls.
A provider without an edit endpoint shows the action as unavailable with the reason.

shopify.text: Native, narrower than first reported: the media editor "might suggest alt text for images where alt text isn't already filled in" (one image at a time, 512 characters allowed). Bulk AI alt text across a catalogue is done by third-party apps.

criteria: A library picture without alt text gets an AI-written one in the main language and in each of the store's languages, told the store's name and where the picture is used.
Staff's alt texts are never written over by the AI; a picture is described again when the store gains a language.
The site shows library alt text wherever a picture has none of its own, in the shopper's language.
Without a model that sees pictures nothing is written and the reason is given.

shopify.text: Native. Semantic Search is AI-powered storefront search that understands intent; the 2024 changelog says merchants on the Shopify or Advanced plan can enable it, and the Search & Discovery page limits it to under 200,000 products on Grow, Advanced and Plus (not Japanese).

criteria: Keyword search (stemmed per locale, trigram typo tolerance) works with no AI and is the fallback whenever the model is unavailable.
Search by meaning merges keyword and vector results by reciprocal rank fusion and compares only vectors of the same space.
Query understanding turns a sentence into filters only through cleanFilters (the store's own slugs, prices to minor units in code); the model never names products or prices.
A search test can be run with the unit being the search, setting no cookie.

shopify.text: Native, as the free Shopify-built Search & Discovery app: related products (purchase history, product description for English storefronts, related collections) and complementary products, with up to 10 manual picks.

criteria: A product grid with a recommendation source shows a cached stand-in for everyone and swaps in the shopper's own, using no cookie and no AI for the stand-in.
Candidates come only from the store's data and every product passes recommendable() and the exclusions (anchors, cart, already bought, never-with).
The model only reorders ids it was given (parseRerank), through the metered connection, under the owner's token cap, and never for the held-out arm.
The effect is measured on tabs with a minimum sample, and past orders can be replayed without learning from the order being checked.

shopify.text: Native (Shopify Inbox, opt-in). The Inbox agent chats with customers automatically and answers questions about products, shipping, returns, sizing and store policies from the catalogue, policies, knowledge bases and web search; existing conversations stay with staff until it is switched on.

gap: D81 and D216 (docs/support.md, steps 1-14): the chat keeps its conversations on the site; a visitor asks for a person and a store's people answer in a shared inbox (or the AI hands over when it cannot help, the tone falls, or it reaches its limit), with email follow-up when nobody is online; a signed-in customer's orders, returns, bookings, subscriptions and bonus are answered from read-only tools (support-tools.ts) through cleanReply(), with link chips made by code; the AI proposes self-service actions the customer confirms and passes other requests to staff. What keeps it partial: the consumer texts of docs/support.md section 8 need human legal review before the row is rated full. Proposed criteria change (docs/support.md 1.5; the criteria themselves are not edited here): order status only to a customer proven by an emailed code or a signed-in session, since an order number with an email proves nothing.
criteria: A visitor can ask for a human: the transcript and the visitor's own typed contact address reach the store's chosen recipients by email, once, and the visitor is told so.
Order status is answered only after the visitor gives the order number and the order's email; a wrong number and a wrong email get the same answer, and no cookie or storage is set.
The model gets the order's facts from a tool (status, shipments, return state) and never states anything the tool did not return; the reply passes cleanReply.
Return and withdrawal policy answers come from store settings (returnFacts) and the agent links the withdrawal page; this already holds.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick in the theme editor). AI block generation, powered by Sidekick, works with every Theme Store theme since 10 December 2025: describe a design, Sidekick writes the block and can be iterated. Sidekick writes copy but is reported (secondary sources) not to build whole pages.

gap: The AI page studio (D92) interviews, plans sections from PATTERNS, writes the words, builds rows and makes the pictures as a draft, plus Make my page cool (D128), AI page translation and copying another site's page (D150); the builder's picture fields make and remake a picture from a description in the site's look (D283). Since D308 (A2) the AI manager builds a page from a brief and changes an existing page from a person's words (edit_page: texts through mapTexts() and replaceInPage() and the row edits, tried first by dryRunEdits(), saved as a draft by savePage(); publishing gated; src/server/site-tools.ts), and since D310 it photographs the draft on a phone and a computer and fixes what the checks find before asking to publish; since A4 it chooses among made themes and presets (list_themes, add_theme, try_theme, make_theme_live). Still short: (1) a described change is saved as a draft from the assistant's panel, not applied unsaved in the open builder (criterion 1); (2) nothing changes a theme's settings from a description ('use warmer colours'): the AI can only pick an existing theme or preset (criterion 2); (3) no whole-store redesign.
criteria: In the builder an owner can describe a change to the open page; the model returns a validated plan of edits on existing parts and it is applied to the editor unsaved, so nothing is saved or published until the owner saves.
A theme change request returns only ThemeSettings values checked by parseStoreTheme, previewed and applied only on the owner's yes.
Every text passes the claims filter, links go only to SiteFacts.links, and a model never writes CSS or script.
Without AI the studio says so and the builder is unchanged.

shopify.text: Native, as the free Shopify-built Translate & Adapt app: automatic translation (the listing says auto-translate up to two languages for free, 20 languages listed), a side-by-side editor and market adaptation.

criteria: From /admin/{store}/translate the owner gets suggestions for products, menus and pages that a person reads and ticks before applyTranslations writes them.
Pages are only saved as drafts; legal texts and a product's safety information start unticked.
Interface text of languages beyond the hand-written ones is translated by AI into the catalogue from the English messages, read key by key, and the languages offered are a platform setting.
Every translation answer is checked (shape, length, claims) and an AI failure leaves the English text.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). Generates ShopifyQL queries and custom data explorations from a question.

gap: The assistant answers only from fixed, code-counted tools: analytics_overview, explain_change, analytics_alerts, sales_summary, sales_trend, sales_funnel, product_performance, customer_insights, restock_suggestions, search_insights, cart_reminder_stats, vat_report and oss_return_data among them (D104, D152, D161). No arbitrary cut (by variant, category, channel, country, payment method), no saved or custom report and no query layer for the model to use; the analytics pages are fixed views, and the report builder this would rest on is missing.
criteria: Over a safe query layer (a typed spec, never free SQL) the assistant can answer a question that cuts a figure by dimension and period; amounts are per currency with a counted note for currencies without a rate.
A figure that cannot be known is returned as what is missing and how to add it, never as zero, and every number is counted in code.
The owner can save an answer as a report that reruns on fresh data, and it shows its definition.
Every report query takes the store id and runs through setBased().

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). Creates customer segments from a natural-language prompt, on top of the rule-based segment editor.

gap: D296: rule-based segments (orders, spend, dates, country, group, RFM class, tags) saved per store, matched in code each time they are read, never readable on the shopper's side (criteria 1 and 4). D297: a broadcast's audience can be a segment, sent only to subscribed addresses (criterion 3; a discount code still reaches groups and named customers only, D299). Since D318 the AI manager lists segments with their counts (list_segments) and drafts a broadcast for one. Still missing (criterion 2): the assistant turning a sentence into a rule set; no tool makes or changes a segment.
criteria: An owner can build a segment from rules (orders, spend, dates, country, group, RFM class, tags) and save it; the member count and list are worked out in code.
The assistant turns a sentence into a rule set that passes the same validation as the editor; the model never lists customers or counts them.
A segment can be used as the audience of a broadcast or a discount, and only customers who consented are mailed.
A segment's list is store-owned, left out of the export unless asked, and never readable on the shopper's side.

history.why: No criterion holds; RFM counts are credited in analytics.rfm-segments-and-customer-lists, and there is no segment builder for the assistant to fill

D296 (wave 5 unit B): saved rule-based segments over customers and subscribers, counted live with a member list, and customer tags; read segments.ts and ran segments.test.ts, segments.int.test.ts (PGlite and integration, passed).

shopify.text: Native (Shopify Flow). Workflows are made manually in a drag-and-drop editor with triggers, conditions and actions, from templates, or by describing them to Sidekick (desktop only); a generated workflow starts inactive and tagged sidekick. The page does not state plan availability.

gap: D238's order rules (Settings -> Automation, src/lib/order-rules.ts, src/server/order-rules.ts, src/components/admin/automation/) are an owner-made workflow for one trigger: when an order is paid (RULE_EVENTS), up to ten conditions from a closed list (total, country, buyer, first order, product, delivery, backorder, gift, source, tag, seller, Stripe risk) and actions tag, notify staff, hold fulfilment and ask the AI manager (D318); saved, switched on and off and ordered, at most 50 a store and 20 AI asks a day, each run logged with what each condition and action came to. Still missing: other triggers (customer, stock, return events), actions that email a customer, call a webhook, post to Slack or create a task, a test run before switching a rule on, and the assistant drafting a rule from a description (order_rules is a read-only tool; rules are made only on the Automation page). Outbound webhooks (D41) and Slack (D101) are credited in platform.outgoing-webhooks; the autopilot's plans (D309) are one-off steps toward goals, not event workflows.
criteria: An owner can create a workflow of one trigger (an order, customer, stock or return event), conditions on its data and actions (email, tag, webhook, Slack, create a task), save it inactive, test it and activate it.
Runs are logged with their result, retried, bounded per store, and can be switched off; an action that sends or spends follows the same gates as the assistant.
The assistant turns a description into a draft workflow that is validated like a hand-made one and always starts inactive.

history.why: No builder exists; the webhook queue is credited in platform.outgoing-webhooks

Read src/lib/order-rules.ts, src/server/order-rules.ts and Settings -> Automation (D238): an owner-made trigger-condition-action rule for one trigger (order paid), a closed list of conditions, actions tag, notify staff, hold and ask the AI manager (D318), saved on or off, at most 50 a store, every run logged in order_rule_runs; held by src/lib/order-rules.test.ts, src/server/order-rules.int.test.ts (run, passing) and e2e/signed-in/automation.spec.ts. Criteria 1 and 2 hold in part; criterion 3 (AI drafts a workflow) is not built: order_rules is a read-only tool.

feature: Create discounts and campaigns from a prompt

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). Creates amount-off product, amount-off order and free-shipping discounts from a prompt.

criteria: The owner asks in words and create_discount or create_campaign is kept as a pending approval with a summary written from the arguments; it runs exactly that call on the owner's yes.
Arguments are validated like the forms (percent, dates, scope, limits) and a campaign works out in the cart and placeOrder the same way.
set_discount_active and set_campaign_active switch them off by chat, also gated.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick with Shopify Messaging). Assists with email campaigns: text, design elements and image insertion.

gap: D297: the broadcast editor's Write with AI (suggestBroadcast()) suggests a subject, preview, heading, paragraphs and a button's words in the chosen language from the staff's own words, every text through findClaims() (a claim refuses the suggestion), never saved or sent; the person sends with their own press, only to subscribed addresses with an unsubscribe link. Since D318 the AI manager drafts one too (draft_broadcast, for everyone or one segment, saved as a draft) and sends only behind the send gate (send_broadcast). Still missing (criterion 1): writing from the store's own facts through tools (products, campaigns); the writer is given only the staff's words and told never to name a product or price it was not told.
criteria: In the broadcast editor the assistant writes subject, preview text and body for a chosen segment from the store's own facts (products, campaigns), each text passing findClaims.
The draft is only a suggestion in the editor; sending is a gated action and goes only to customers who consented, with an unsubscribe link.
The model is given no prices or stock it was not handed by a tool, and the email's amounts come from the store's data.

history.why: First report's skeptic recheck: the AI manager drafts one email to one customer (`email_customer`), so not missing; the report itself called it thin and effectively missing for campaigns. Entry written in wave 0 from the first report, which did not log it.
email_customer is a one-customer gated mail, not a marketing email; no criterion holds
D297: Write with AI in the broadcast editor suggests the email's words through the claims filter, as a suggestion only; it does not yet read the store's products or campaigns.

shopify.text: Native. Products reach ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot and Meta through the Shopify Catalog (Google ones also through Merchant Center); active by default for eligible stores after accepting the supplemental terms, managed under Sales channels > Agentic; ChatGPT is discovery only, other channels can use direct checkout; orders carry channel attribution.

gap: D302 serves a normalised feed per store and market (storeFeed(), src/server/feeds.ts): offered goods only, VAT-inclusive prices in the market's currency as the storefront shows them, as Google Merchant Center RSS (which Google's AI shopping surfaces read) and Meta, TikTok and Pinterest CSVs, every product left out named with its reason on Marketing -> Product feeds; llms.txt, crawler switches and JSON-LD besides (ai.ai-discovery-signals). Still missing: a feed in the AI channels' own specs (ChatGPT, Copilot, Perplexity) and a per-channel opt-in (the feeds are on or off for the store as a whole, criterion 1); attribution of an order to an agent channel (criterion 3). In-chat checkout stays off. Merged on 2026-10-25 (README rule 8): `customers.ai-assistant-discoverability-and-agentic-commerce` was the same Shopify feature (rated partial); its criteria and evidence are here.
criteria: A store can opt in per channel and a normalised product feed is served per market with the attributes each channel requires, only for published products with VAT-inclusive prices in the market's currency.
Products the feed cannot carry are listed in the admin with the reason, and the feed validates against the channel's own spec in a test.
An order that comes from an agent channel is attributed to it in analytics without any cookie or storage.
In-chat checkout stays off until a payment path exists; a channel's switch is per store and defaults to off.

A product feed for AI shopping channels is built from the same normalised list as the Merchant Center feed: price with VAT in the market's currency, availability and images; products not for sale are left out.

A read-only shopper-facing endpoint (MCP or the channels' own protocol) answers catalogue search and product details from the store's own data, without personal data, rate-limited, with checkout staying on the store.
The owner switches each channel off; a switched-off channel gets nothing and robots.txt says so.
Live only once each channel's programme accepts the store (bucket B).

history.why: Read src/server/feeds.ts, src/lib/feeds.ts, src/app/api/feeds/[token]/[file]/route.ts and the Product feeds page (D302): a normalised feed per store and market of offered goods at the storefront's VAT-inclusive price, as Google Merchant Center RSS (read by Google's AI shopping surfaces) and Meta, TikTok and Pinterest CSVs, with every product left out listed with its reason; held by src/lib/feeds.test.ts and src/server/feeds.int.test.ts (run, passing). The gap's 'no feed' no longer holds; no feed in an AI channel's own spec, no per-channel opt-in and no agent-channel attribution, so partial.

shopify.text: Native. Every store's UCP discovery profile is at /.well-known/ucp and its MCP endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp (Catalog tools search_catalog, lookup_catalog, get_product; Cart tools; Checkout); UCP replaces the deprecated Storefront MCP, and agents send an agent profile with each request. Shopify manages agents.md for every store by default.

gap: `/api/mcp` serves the owner tools to Kaizen Life only (D96) and answers 401 without a Kaizen Life token. The WordPress plugin's API (D169, D170: products, terms, a cart quote and a hand-off to the store's own checkout) answers only a site an owner connected, with that connection's token. There is no public, rate-limited endpoint for shopping agents, no /.well-known/ucp profile and no /agents.md; agents get llms.txt, JSON-LD and the product feeds (D302) only.
criteria: A store serves a discovery profile and a public MCP endpoint whose catalog tools (search, lookup, get product) answer from the store's published products only, with the market's VAT-inclusive prices and stock as available or not.
The endpoint is rate-limited, returns no personal data, sets no cookie, and obeys the store's per-bot switches.
A create-cart tool hands back the store's own checkout address; nothing is paid or ordered through the endpoint.
The owner MCP at /api/mcp is unchanged and still refuses any token but Kaizen Life's.

shopify.text: Native, from Shopify's own documentation: Shopify manages an agents.md for every store by default (theme templates agents.md.liquid, llms.txt.liquid and llms-full.txt.liquid can override), with llms.txt and llms-full.txt mirroring it and pointing to the UCP and MCP endpoints.

criteria: Each store and Kaizen serve /llms.txt listing the open store's products and pages with the owner's own text, and leave out a hidden store.
robots.txt carries per-bot switches for AI assistants and AI training crawlers and the owner's extra rules, written under the store's address and checked for what it cannot read.
Products, pages, articles and the organisation carry JSON-LD.

shopify.text: Native (Sidekick). "Sidekick can also work with third-party apps to answer questions and complete tasks."

gap: No app ecosystem, so nothing can add tools to the assistant; the tool catalogue is in code (OWNER_TOOLS). Only Kaizen Life reaches it from outside, through the owner-only MCP (D96). Depends on the extension-platform decision (plan section 5, decision 2).
criteria: An owner can register a custom app with scoped tokens whose tools the assistant may call, each switched on by the owner.
A custom app's tools are read-only unless declared gated; a gated call is only kept for the owner's yes.
Calls to a custom app are metered, time-limited and logged, and an app's answer is treated as data, never as instructions.

feature: AI controls, usage and cost visibility

shopify.text: Native, narrower: merchants choose which agentic channels take part under Sales channels > Agentic and see search and sales performance of products there; Sidekick image generation has plan-dependent monthly and short-term limits. No per-call token or cost view was found on the pages read.

criteria: Every model call goes through metered() and is recorded for the store the connection was made for, with the feature it was for, and the owner sees usage and the platform sees all of it.

Cost uses the price in force when the call was made, from a price table the platform admin keeps; pictures, speech and live calls have their own units; a model with no price shows as no price and totals carry a plus, never as free.
A store can use its own provider and key instead of Kaizen's, and Kaizen never names a provider or model in code.
